targets.name: Octavia E. Butler Landing
targets.summary: Perseverance touchdown site, 18 Feb 2021. Flat, fractured basaltic lava plain; the MOXIE experiment later produced oxygen from the CO₂ atmosphere on this crater floor, the first in-situ resource demonstration on another planet.

targets.name: Roubion · Polygon Valley
targets.summary: First coring attempt of the mission. The altered basalt crumbled to powder — evidence of extensive aqueous weathering — and the tube sealed a sample of Martian atmosphere instead.

targets.name: Rochette · Citadelle
targets.summary: First rock cores collected on Mars (Montdenier, Montagnac). Basaltic lava with salt-filled voids: an igneous rock datable on Earth that also records later contact with liquid water.

targets.name: Brac outcrop · South Séítah
targets.summary: Olivine-rich cumulate, formed when crystals settled in a thick magma body. Olivine is partly altered to carbonate — a reaction that consumes water and CO₂ and can release hydrogen.

targets.name: Issole · Séítah
targets.summary: Second Séítah sampling station (Robine, Malay cores). Layered olivine cumulate ridges separated by sand ripples; ripples and ledges make this the roughest ground on the crater floor.

targets.name: Three Forks sample depot
targets.summary: Ten sealed sample tubes were laid on the surface here as a backup cache for Mars Sample Return. Chosen because it is flat and rock-poor: a proven safe landing and staging zone at the foot of the delta.

targets.name: Amalik · Cape Nukshak
targets.summary: Fine-grained sedimentary rocks at the base of the delta scarp (Shuyak, Mageik cores). Lowest exposed beds of the lake-deposited sequence, with sulfate and clay minerals.

targets.name: Wildcat Ridge · Hogwallow Flats
targets.summary: Sulfate-bearing mudstone deposited in still lake water. SHERLOC measured the mission's strongest organic-associated signals to that date here; fine mudstones are the best preservers of biosignatures.

targets.name: Belva crater overlook
targets.summary: Rim of a ~0.9 km impact crater that punches into the fan top. Its walls expose steeply dipping sandstone beds and boulders, a natural cross-section through the river deposits.

targets.name: Onahu · Upper fan
targets.summary: Conglomerate of rounded pebbles carried by a fast river from far outside the crater (Otis Peak core): a grab-bag of rocks from the ancient highlands watershed.

targets.name: Pelican Point · Margin unit
targets.summary: First station in the carbonate-rich band along the inner crater edge, mapped from orbit by CRISM. Carbonates precipitate from water and can entomb organic matter.

targets.name: Bunsen Peak · Margin unit
targets.summary: Carbonate and silica cemented rock (Comet Geyser core). Both minerals are excellent at preserving microfossils and organics on Earth.

targets.name: Bright Angel · Cheyava Falls
targets.summary: Mudstone in the inlet river channel with 'leopard spot' reaction fronts of iron phosphate and iron sulfide associated with organic carbon (Sapphire Canyon core) — reported as a potential biosignature that requires sample return to resolve.

targets.name: Lookout Hill · Crater rim
targets.summary: Highest point of the Perseverance traverse, about 780 m above the landing site. Commands a view of the whole crater floor and delta; the climb sustains the steepest slopes of the mission.

targets.name: Witch Hazel Hill
targets.summary: Layered outcrop on the outer rim exposing some of the oldest rocks sampled on Mars (Silver Mountain core), uplifted from deep crust by the Jezero impact.
